Evidence:
[1] Tartaric acid is a white crystalline organic acid that occurs naturally in many plants, most notably in grapes. Its salt, potassium bitartrate, commonly known as cream of tartar, develops naturally in the process of winemaking.
[2] Heat is used to increase the solubility of humic acids and hence more potassium humate can be extracted.
[3] In cooking it is known as cream of tartar.
[4] A marshmallow is a sugar-based confection that, in its modern form, typically consists of sugar, water and gelatin which is whipped to a spongy consistency, molded into small cylindrical pieces, and coated with corn starch.

Notes:
[bridge] Potassium bitartrate, also known as cream of tartar, is a key ingredient in the Scottish confection Edinburgh rock.
